question.problem: If ${X}_{1}∼N(2,{4}^{2})$ and ${X}_{2}∼N(3,{2}^{2})$, then what is the distribution of $Y={X}_{1}-{X}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent random variables, where ${X}_{1}∼N({\mu }_{1},{\sigma }_{1}^{2})$ and ${X}_{2}∼N({\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2}),$  then 

$$
{X}_{1}-{X}_{2}∼N({\mu }_{1}-{\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{\sigma }_{2}^{2}).
$$

However, in this case, we don't know whether ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent. Therefore, we do not have enough information to determine the answer.
